messages:
maya: Quick summary of the onboarding scan for the new 8b vs 14b variants — ran quant experiments (int4/int8) across the QA + instruction suites. posting the short econ + routing recs. :eyes:

kevin: numbers first?

maya: yes. aggregated numbers (prod-like prompts, 2k token budget):
- 8b int4: p50 latency 120ms, p95 420ms, avg tokens/sec 75, unit cost ~ $0.12 / 1k tokens, instr helpfulness 0.76, math accuracy 0.61
- 14b int8: p50 latency 210ms, p95 680ms, avg tokens/sec 40, unit cost ~ $0.33 / 1k tokens, instr helpfulness 0.79, math accuracy 0.72

kevin: delta: 14b buys ~+0.03 instr helpfulness, +0.11 math accuracy at ~2.75x cost. latency roughly 1.75x.

toni: product question — is the quality gap visible for short chat prompts or only long-context / math-style queries?

maya: short chit-chat: negligible perceived difference. For step-by-step reasoning and math, 14b consistently outperforms. Domain tests (support KB) show mixed results — many retrieval-heavy prompts do fine on 8b.

sara: GTM asks what we should set as default model for new customers on hosted tiers?

kevin: baseline rec: set 8b int4 as default for non-premium / interactive chat workflows. Reasons: 3x better token econ, similar UX for the majority of queries. Use 14b int8 as a higher-quality tier for: premium users, long reasoning chains, and paid features (summaries that must be precise).

maya: operational notes: int4 path needs extra headroom in batching to avoid IO stalls — we saw spikes when batch sizes > 48 for certain token shapes. Also KV cache memory footprint smaller on int4 which helps throughput.

kevin: routing config prototype (canary):
```
route_rules:
  - name: long_context_or_premium
    condition: request.tokens > 512 OR user.tier == 'premium'
    target: model:14b-int8
  - name: default_lowcost
    condition: otherwise
    target: model:8b-int4
fallbacks:
  - if: model_unavailable
    to: 8b-int4
    notify: ops_team
```

toni: can we do an A/B where 10% of non-premium traffic goes to 14b to measure NPS / escalation rate?

maya: yes. small canary for 14b on low-risk cohorts. metrics to track: token cost delta, avg latency, user-rated helpfulness sample, support escalations per 10k sessions.

sara: pricing implication note for GTM deck: if default is 8b-int4, we can advertise 2-3x cheaper average token cost vs our high-quality tier. need an exact figure for slides.

kevin: use token-econ calc: assume 1k tokens per session => 8b-int4 $0.12, 14b-int8 $0.33 => ~175% incremental cost. For 100k sessions: incremental monthly $$ = (0.33-0.12) * 100k = $21,000. Add GPU infra ops premium for spiky tails.

maya: caveats: quant regressions appeared on a small subset of syntax-heavy prompts (code generation with unusual tokens). we patched tokenizer normalization and re-ran; residual errors down to <0.5% of calls. recommend keeping a small prompt-level evalset to catch regressions after quant changes.

ops-bot: deploy-check OK for canary config. No resource conflicts flagged.

kevin: rollout plan (short):
1) create canary route (10% non-premium -> 14b) for 2 weeks
2) collect metrics + human ratings + support logs
3) if math / reason improvement > 8% absolute and cost per positive-outcome < target, expand to premium product and update pricing.

maya: tl;dr recs: default to 8b-int4 for interactive workloads, route by token length and premium flag to 14b-int8 for heavy reasoning or paid tiers. enable prompt-level regression tests and a small canary A/B.

toni: sounds good. I'll file a short PRD and tag eng on the routing change. :+1:

sara: will update GTM materials once we get canary numbers.

maya: added the eval artifacts to the model-onboard bucket and a short runbook for rollback. ping me for links if you need them.

kevin: thanks — will draft the rollout playbook and ETA the next steps tomorrow.

maya: end.
